record.paper_title: Mini-Proceedings ECT* Workshop: Hadronic Atoms and Kaonic Nuclei
record.original_question: What real and imaginary K−p scattering lengths, K−n scattering information, and isospin-dependent antikaon-nucleon scattering lengths are consistent with kaonic hydrogen and kaonic deuterium measurements, low-energy K−p data, and πΣ mass spectra, and how should those data constrain subthreshold antikaon-nucleon interaction amplitudes used in kaonic-nucleus calculations?

evidence.quote: The kaonic hydrogen was measured by the DEAR Collaboration (on DAΦNE) with an unprecedented precision, leading to a lively debate on the kaon-proton scattering length extraction procedure, and on the compatibility with existent kaon-nucleon scattering data.

the corresponding observables of kaonic deuterium are a hot topic since they are necessary to extract the isospin dependent K−-nucleon scattering lengths. For the first time kaonic deuterium was studied by SIDDHARTA very recently. The extraction of the scattering lengths is subject of intense theoretical work
The K−p scattering lengths deduced from these measurements are not fully consistent: a(K−p) = −0.47 (±0.10) + i 0.30 (±0.17) [fm] [DEAR] and a(K−p) = −0.78 (±0.18) + i 0.49 (±0.37) [fm] [KEK].
With systematic experiments one can extract the K−N scattering amplitudes below the K−N threshold down to about -35 MeV. At this moment one has only K1H [1] and K4He [2] data.

artifact.status_search_result: Following the question's posing, the SIDDHARTA measurement of kaonic hydrogen at DAΦNE substantially reduced the K^-p scattering-length uncertainty and is now widely used (together with πΣ spectra and low-energy K^-p data) in chiral coupled-channel analyses to pin down a_0, a_1, and the subthreshold \bar K N amplitudes. However, kaonic deuterium has not yet been measured with comparable precision (SIDDHARTA-2 aims at this), so the isospin-1 scattering length a_1 and the subthreshold extrapolation of \bar K N amplitudes used in kaonic-nucleus calculations remain only partially constrained.

status_evidence.title: Kaon–nucleon scattering lengths from kaonic deuterium experiments revisited
status_evidence.snippet: Extraction of isospin-dependent KN scattering lengths from kaonic hydrogen and kaonic deuterium measurements requires improved deuterium data.
status_evidence.claim: Isospin-dependent KN scattering lengths still require precise kaonic deuterium measurements; only partial extraction is possible from existing data.

status_evidence.title: Kaonic Atoms Measurement at DAΦNE: SIDDHARTA and SIDDHARTA-2
status_evidence.snippet: SIDDHARTA performed the most precise kaonic hydrogen measurement; SIDDHARTA-2 is dedicated to the first precise kaonic deuterium measurement.
status_evidence.claim: Kaonic hydrogen has been measured with high precision (SIDDHARTA), while kaonic deuterium precision measurement is the goal of SIDDHARTA-2 (still ongoing).

status_evidence.title: The studies of kaonic atoms at DAΦNE: from SIDDHARTA to SIDDHARTA-2
status_evidence.snippet: Coupled-channel chiral analyses constrained by SIDDHARTA improved the determination of \bar K N subthreshold amplitudes.
status_evidence.claim: Subthreshold \bar K N amplitudes are now better constrained but still depend on forthcoming kaonic deuterium data.
